lesson.title: Inserting and Removing List Items
lesson.driving_question: How can a program place a new item at a chosen position or remove a known value?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Changing list membership by value and chosen position
lesson.concept_budget: Insert one item at a position and remove one known existing value; missing-value handling is deferred.
misconceptions: insert() uses a position and a value.
remove() uses a value, not a position.
remove() deletes the first matching value.
lesson.progression_note: Adds two required list-editing methods before contrasting value removal with positional deletion.

shared_program.filename: Inserting and Removing List Items - Starter Code.py
shared_program.code:
kit = ["coat", "water", "torch"]
kit.insert(1, "map")
kit.remove("coat")
print("Packed kit:", kit)

primm.prompt: Recall that list positions start at 0 and that a method call names the list before the dot.
Trace the list once after insert() and again after remove(). Write the final order without skipping either state.
Run the supplied file, then change the insert position to 0. Compare how the order shifts.

questions: Why does insert() take a position first but remove() takes a stored value?
What happens if remove() is given a value that is not in the list?
After map is inserted and coat is removed, what exact list is printed and which position contains map?

primm.prompt: Insert "snack" at position 2 and keep the removal of coat. The final order must be water, snack, torch.

Ask for an item and store it in [new_item], then insert it at position 1. Display the list after the insertion. Ask for an existing item and store it in [old_item], then remove it and display the list again. Test "map" followed by "coat".

Store "Ari", "Bao", "Cleo" and "Dara" in [runners]. Ask for an insertion position from 0 to 4 and store it in [position]. Ask for a reserve name and store it in [reserve], then insert it at [position]. Ask for an existing name and store it in [leaving], then remove it. Use a for loop to display each remaining name. Test position 1, reserve "Eli" and leaving name "Bao"; display Ari, Eli, Cleo and Dara on separate lines.
Repair the argument order for insert() and give remove() the item value rather than its position.

programs.challenge2:
kit = ["coat", "water", "torch"]
new_item = input("Item to insert: ")
kit.insert(1, new_item)
print("After insert:", kit)
old_item = input("Existing item to remove: ")
kit.remove(old_item)
print("After remove:", kit)

runners.remove(leaving)
print("Runners:", runners)
